title: Hyperelliptic Jacobian arithmetic
objective: Implement canonical genus-2/3 Jacobian divisor classes, odd-degree Cantor group law, scalar arithmetic, orders/basic structure where feasible, exhaustive law tests, and benchmarks in ordinary Python

handoff.summary: Implemented ordinary-Python genus-2/3 odd-degree Mumford divisors, generalized Cantor composition/reduction for y^2+h*y=f, exact scalar and element orders, Frobenius-derived Jacobian extension orders, practical point/random sampling, bounded enumeration and invariant factors, and an exact one-sided order-candidate filter. Sage differential vectors, h!=0 collisions, 256-bit scalars, cyclic/noncyclic groups, exhaustive small-field laws, and GF(9) polynomial fallback pass.
risks: Characteristic 2 is explicitly unsupported because smooth models require the unimplemented even-degree infinity representation.
Even-degree split/inert Jacobians and certified embedded abelian-group generators remain unimplemented.
Generic group_structure() is deliberately exhaustive and resource-capped; it is a small-workload correctness fallback, not a production large-field algorithm.
architecture:check reaches the native gate but currently fails on unclassified files introduced by the rebased smalljac lane; test:native was therefore not rerun in this lane.
next_steps: Integrate the curve model's C.jacobian() lazy hook and run the combined public API/oracle suite.
Use elements_from_points() or random_elements() with filter_order_candidates() in the genus-3 exact-completion lane.
Run the focused suite on Windows x64, macOS arm64, and Linux arm64 after integration.
Implement the extended (u,v,n) representation before enabling even-degree or characteristic-2 Jacobian arithmetic.
